title: Mysuru Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
**Pricing power is thin and set by the OEM** — ICRA notes high competitive intensity forces high operational efficiency [8], and CRISIL flags that suppliers of engine and related parts carry higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. So when a proposal lands, check the customer mix and the part family before the balance sheet. ## Where the cash actually sits
**Gross current assets have averaged 160-170 days in recent years [10]** — that is the real lending need, not the machine. **Margin is squeezed from the input side**: ASK Automotive reported record revenue but aluminium squeezing margins [5], and Elara expects strong Q4FY26 volumes with margins under pressure from commodity risk [6]. So ask for the hedging policy on aluminium and steel; if the unit is unhedged and sells on fixed-price annual contracts, price the risk in or decline. **Capex should be customer-backed** — a new line only against a named OEM nomination letter, never speculative. ## What has changed now
**Karnataka is outrunning India: GST collections +11.1% Apr-to-date vs +6.1% [D], and electricity demand +23.3% vs +9.5% [D].** Nationally, IIP for NIC 29 auto output is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D]. **Peer results confirm the volume pull**: Motherson Sumi Wiring net profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore on revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], and Lumax Auto beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its outlook [7]. **Local news is thin on components specifically** — a Hyundai Bayon launch at a Mysuru dealer [3] and a proposed ARAI centre in neighbouring Mandya [2] are demand and ecosystem signals, not order books. Treat them as sentiment, not collateral. ## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue tier-2 component makers with two or more OEM customers, EV-agnostic or EV-leaning product lines, and a nomination pipeline.** ASK's order wins span EV braking and aluminium lightweighting [5] — that is the shape to back. **Avoid single-OEM dependent units, engine/diesel-injection specialists with no EV plan [11], and any borrower whose receivables are stretching beyond the 160-170 day norm [10].**

## How to grow safely
**Structure as cash-flow lending against receivables, not clean term debt.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, a quarterly drawing-power reconciliation, and a covenant capping Debt/EBITDA — rating guidance flags stress above 2.5-2.75 times [10]. **Take the OEM nomination letters and the hedging confirmations every quarter.** If receivables cross 170 days, ask for the ageing and the top-buyer payment record before any enhancement.

## Early warning signs to watch
- **Receivable days drifting past 170 [10]** — ask for buyer-wise ageing and stop enhancement. - **Unhedged aluminium/steel exposure on fixed-price contracts [5][6]** — demand a hedge or reprice the facility. - **Customer concentration above two-thirds in one OEM** — seek a second nomination before renewal. - **Engine-part-only product mix with no EV roadmap [11]** — shorten tenor and raise margin.
